1. Propositions and conjectures

In this section we collect the propositions and conjectures that motivate the rest of the paper. Each is stated without proof; the proofs (where available) appear in subsequent sections.

Proposition 1.1 (Flatness criterion).

A finitely generated module $M$ over a Noetherian ring $R$ is flat if and only if $\mathrm{Tor}_1^R(M, N) = 0$ for every finitely generated $R$-module $N$.

Proof.

The forward direction follows from the long exact sequence of $\mathrm{Tor}$. For the converse, write $N$ as a quotient of a free module and apply the snake lemma.

Conjecture 1.2 (Hodge conjecture, restricted).

For a smooth projective variety $X$ over $\mathbb{C}$, every rational $(p,p)$-class is algebraic.

Proposition 1.3.

The étale cohomology of a smooth projective curve of genus $g$ satisfies a Poincaré duality.
